tasks.short: Make minor repairs and report major service needs

steps.what: Assess machine problems and make permitted minor repairs and adjustments
Notify supervisors when observations indicate major service is required

tasks.design: Keep assessment, permitted repairs and escalation with the operator, referring to equipment instructions in {DOCS}. Test native service reporting only if a distinct repeated clerical burden is observed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Faults require physical examination and an understanding of permitted repair scope.
tasks.enabler_now: Document access can support work but does not replace repair or escalation judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising a problem beyond operator competence or authority.
tasks.human_edge: Practical examination and clear communication of the observed fault.
tasks.altitude: Repair and escalation responsibilities remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: The supplied production-record tools do not establish replacement of physical repairs or service escalation judgement.

assumptions: Boundary covers operator minor work and notification; maintenance diagnosis, major repair and supervisor decisions retain their own time.
Operator produces fault observations during s1 and explains them in s2. No machine consumes a free fault code, repairability flag or service severity decision.
Use native reporting first if a clerical subtask emerges.
No new software or capture requirement means zero incremental upkeep.

tasks.previous_blocker: Learning depends on the actual machine, learner understanding and physical demonstration.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital instructions support teaching without proving reduced teaching time.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising misunderstanding during setup or operation.
tasks.human_edge: Adapting instruction to the learner's actions and questions.
tasks.altitude: Instruction and competence observation remain human.

steps.what: Read operational values and capture machine, job, time and units
Transcribe operational data into the production record format
Check recorded values and accept the operational record

tasks.design: Configure native manual entry in {OPS_SYSTEM} so one capture creates the required record layout. Keep reading and context capture fully counted, and let the operator review the staged record before accepting it; no controller feed is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Operators may copy the same readings from a capture sheet into a separate record layout.
tasks.enabler_now: Production records tools support manual entry as well as machine connections.
tasks.still_hard: The correct job, reading unit and timing must match the physical machine state.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising an implausible or contextually misleading reading.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated transcription; physical observation remains unchanged.

evidence.claim: MPDV HYDRA X collects machine quantities and states from controls or manual entry; manual entry support does not establish automatic availability of every pressure or stroke reading.
The proposed single-capture layout removes only repeated transcription, with unmeasured local savings.

assumptions: Boundary is operator operational recording, excluding machine setup, continuous process monitoring and supervisor analysis.

Operator in s1 reads and enters machine ID, job ID, timestamp, parameter name, numeric value, unit and any observation note. This capture retains all 55 hours. Missing or doubtful readings are re-read manually; unavailable form access uses the existing paper route.
The configured form produces s2 directly from those captured entries; no free discrepancy code or sensor signal is assumed. Operator checks final context and values in s3.
Test native forms and output layout first. Already automatic recording earns no saving; employee-linked data access and consultation needs are checked locally.
research_questions: Does single capture reduce transcription after field entry, review and upkeep?

incremental.description: Maintain field definitions and record checks

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=55+0+20=75, gross=25, focal upkeep=7, net=18. Range 0-5 assumes an observed second transcription; existing single entry yields no saving.

steps.what: Interpret part requirements and write programs using the machining software and machine conventions

tasks.enabler_now: Existing machining software supports programming and simulation but does not establish an additional reduction here.
tasks.still_hard: A syntactically valid program can conflict with fixtures or produce the wrong part.
tasks.human_edge: Connecting design intent, workholding and actual machine behaviour.
tasks.altitude: Programming and verification responsibility remains unchanged.

evidence.claim: Existing machining software can support programming; no measured additional repetitive coding subtask is established for this operator task.

assumptions: Boundary ends at an accepted program version, excluding machine setup, proving, physical cutting and production release; those retain their own labour.
